target: a lead-list cleaning CLI with tests, built on a real-shaped provider export
summary: The run wrote a stdlib clean_leads.py and a 12-test suite, and the fixture output (clean.csv) has 7 rows with the info@, gmail and 2,600-employee rows removed. The final report says nothing was executed and gives a hand-reasoned count (6 of 9 rows kept) that contradicts its own list of 7 kept names and the actual 7-row output.

checks.detail: wrote 7 rows to clean.csv; dropped: role_inbox=1, free_mail=1, over_limit=1

checks.desc: drops the info@, gmail and 2,600-employee rows

met: Complete stdlib script with argparse, --max-employees (default 500), -o, and exit code 1 with a stderr message on OSError, ValueError or csv.Error

Tests cover role inboxes (including +tag and a lookalike name), free mail, the 500/501 limit boundary, bad employee counts, case-insensitive dedupe, malformed emails, a CLI end-to-end run, a missing column and a missing file
Edge cases handled: missing required columns, blank or malformed emails, mixed-case emails, UTF-8 BOM, '1,200' and '250.0' employee values, and a filtered row not shadowing a later duplicate
Run steps and a section-by-section plain-English map are given, and the assumptions are flagged
Hard checks pass: the script runs on the fixture and the three target rows are dropped (clean.csv has 7 rows, none of them info@, gmail or the 2,600-employee company)
missed: The final report says nothing was run because Bash was denied, yet the transcript shows a Bash call (tests plus a run on the fixture), so the report does not match what the run did. The user gets no observed test or run results.
The hand-reasoned expectation is wrong: it says 6 of 9 rows are kept but lists 7 names, and the real output has 7 kept rows plus 3 dropped, so the fixture has 10 rows.
One dropped row is shown as a literal '<email>' placeholder instead of the actual address.
No quoted test output or drop-count summary from a real run is included in the report.
skill_defects: The skill has no rule for when verification can't run: it should say to report only what was observed and not to give predicted counts as fact, or to re-read the fixture to get the numbers right.

The skill doesn't tell the agent to reconcile the final report with the tool results, so a report can claim 'not run' while the transcript shows a run, and can give counts that contradict the output files.
The skill doesn't require the final report to quote the actual run output (test summary and drop counts) rather than paraphrase it.
